Why it matters
The Nonfarm Payrolls report is the most closely watched indicator of U.S. labour market health and a key driver of Federal Reserve policy decisions.
Monetary policy. Strong job growth may support higher rates for longer. Weak data may signal easing ahead.
Market volatility. Historically one of the highest volatility events for USD pairs, indices and gold.
Economic health. Reflects business sentiment, consumer spending potential and overall economic momentum.

14:28 (UTC+00:00) · 3 min read
Durable goods orders fall 6.3% in April, less than the 7.8% decline expected
BN
ByteFX Newsdesk
Source: U.S. Census Bureau
◈
⤴
New orders for manufactured durable goods declined 6.3% in April, a smaller drop than the 7.8% consensus and a sharp reversal from the 7.6% rise recorded in March.
Excluding transportation, core orders rose 0.2% against a 0.1% forecast. The transportation component accounted for the bulk of the headline decline, a pattern that repeats whenever aircraft orders swing month to month.
The dollar firmed modestly on the release. EUR/USD held its earlier range, trading near 1.0814, while the two-year Treasury yield was little changed. Rate markets continue to price a hold at the June meeting.
Attention now turns to the Core PCE Price Index due May 24, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge and the more consequential print for the June decision.
The numbers
Actual
-6.3%
Forecast
-7.8%
Previous
+7.6%
A decline that beats a steeper forecast still reads as a beat — colour follows the surprise, not the sign.
